title: Affine-line purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ be the scheme of the
affine-line datum and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=A$. The affine-line purity
comparison $\gamma_{p,K}$ of
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] – the adjoint of the
projection-formula composite
$Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]\cong K\otimes^L Rp_!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\to K$
formed with the projective-line trace and normalized by the orientation
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] – is an isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{p,K}:Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp^!K.
$$

It is natural in $K$ and compatible with arbitrary base change of $Y$.
(Source: the relative affine-line case of cohomological purity, as in
Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and
16.7 and Proposition 16.11, with the acyclicity computation of Example
16.3 and the Gysin sequence of the divisor, over an arbitrary base
scheme.)

proof.text: Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, and write $a:X\hookrightarrow P$ for the compactifying open immersion (distinct from the punctured-line immersion in the affine-line datum), so $p=qa$. The hypotheses of [def-pur-affine-line-datum] include $Y$ separated finite type over $k$, $A=A_{E,n}$, $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, and $\ell\ne p_{\mathrm{char}}$. Hence $Y,X,P$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the spectrum of the field and then to the polynomial charts. Put $r=n/e$ and $m=\ell^r$, so $mA=0$ and $m$ is invertible on all these schemes. The specified pro-etale twist agrees with the realization of the ordinary etale twist $\mu_m\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A$ by [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]; it is locally free of rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Choose a bounded constructible ordinary-etale representative $K_0$ and $\alpha:\nu_Y^*K_0\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Its finite Tor amplitude is that of $K$, by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]. The same applies after pullback along $p,q,a$: [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives finite Tor amplitude and constructibility on the pro-etale site, and the origin and Tor-comparison statements give the corresponding properties on the etale representatives. Tensoring with the locally free rank-one twist is exact locally and only shifts the cohomological and Tor intervals by $[2]$. No preservation theorem for $Rp^!$ is being assumed. Applied to $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] supplies a finite integer $d$ bounding $\dim P$ (the unique fibre is $P$); this verifies the compactification-dimension hypothesis of the actual-adjoint comparison used in Step 5. The same argument applies over any base $Y'$ in the chapter setting.

source.place: Proof, coefficient conventions; unit sk-prop-an Step 5(c)

proof.text:
Work first on the ordinary etale sites. Set $T_P=A_P(1)[2]$, $T_X=a^*T_P$, $G_q(L)=q^*L\otimes_A^LT_P$, and $G_p(L)=a^*G_q(L)=p^*L(1)[2]$. By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], $Rq_*\dashv G_q$ with actual counit $\epsilon_{q,L}=(1_L\otimes t_q)\pi_q^{-1}$. By [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], $Da_!\dashv a^*$ on the entire ordinary derived categories; denote its evaluation counit by $e_a$. The compactification formula [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $F_p=Rq_*Da_!$. Compose these two adjunctions using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. It gives $F_p\dashv G_p$ with actual counit
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,L}=\epsilon_{q,L}\circ Rq_*(e_{a,G_qL}):Rq_*Da_!a^*G_qL\longrightarrow L.$$
Thus the adjunction includes its counit, not just the existence of a right adjoint.

source.place: Proof, explicit projective-line adjunction and its restriction; unit Step 5(c)

proof.text:
Identify this counit at $L=K_0$. Let $u:Da_!T_X\to T_P$ be $e_{a,T_P}$ and put $\int_p=t_q\circ Rq_*u$. Write $\rho:Da_!a^*(q^*K_0\otimes^LT_P)\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*K_0\otimes^LDa_!T_X$ for the inverse open projection map, with the tensor symmetry understood. Its invertibility is the case $f=a$ of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]; the same node for $f=p$ gives the compact-support projection isomorphism. The open evaluation satisfies
$$e_{a,q^*K_0\otimes T_P}=(1_{q^*K_0}\otimes u)\rho.$$
Indeed the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is identity on every etale test object factoring through $X$; on such an object the displayed equation sends $x\otimes t$ to $x\otimes t$, and on the zero-extension presheaf's other components both maps are zero. This also proves the equality on flat representatives used for derived tensor. By the compactification definition of the projection map [def-exchange-projection], its inverse at $T_X,K_0$ is $\pi_q(Da_!T_X)^{-1}\circ Rq_*\rho$. Naturality of the proper projection isomorphism [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] with respect to $u$ therefore gives
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,K_0}=(1_{K_0}\otimes t_q)\pi_q(T_P)^{-1}Rq_*(1\otimes u)Rq_*\rho
=(1_{K_0}\otimes\int_p)\pi_q(Da_!T_X)^{-1}Rq_*\rho.$$
This is precisely the projection-formula integration composite defining the comparison in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison].

source.place: Proof, identification of the composite counit; unit Step 5(b),(c)

proof.text: Let $p^\times$ be the ordinary etale right adjoint supplied by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] for the fixed compactification $(a,q)$. Compare $F_p\dashv G_p$ of Step 2 with $F_p\dashv p^\times$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to the identity isomorphism of their common left adjoint $F_p$. Its conjugate $\delta:G_p\xrightarrow{\sim}p^\times$ is a natural isomorphism, and its component $\delta_{K_0}$ is the transpose of $\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,K_0}$ under $F_p\dashv p^\times$ (the formula for the conjugate is the unit followed by the image of this counit). Step 3 identifies that counit with integration. Consequently it is the specified comparison, rather than merely some isomorphism between the same two objects, that is invertible on the etale site. Naturality is also obtained here from the natural transformation $\delta$.

source.place: Proof, uniqueness of right adjoints with the specified counit; unit Step 5(c)

proof.text:
Realize Step 4 on the pro-etale site. The compact-support comparison [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies $Rp_!
u_X^*M$ with $
u_Y^*F_pM$ for bounded-below $M$. The unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies $R
u_{Y,*}K$ with $K_0$ via the witness $\alpha$. Under these identifications [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives exactly the transported adjunction bijection with right adjoint $
u_X^*p^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$. The comparison inverse image is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]; its tensor comparison is the ringed-topos isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The inverse-image squares commute because the inclusions defining [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] commute with base change of etale schemes: both composites send a test scheme to its fibre product with the same scheme. Together with the twist identification of Step 1, these give $
u_X^*G_pK_0\cong Lp^*K(1)[2]$. Applying the transported Hom bijection to the counit calculated in Step 3 thus gives precisely $\gamma_{p,K}$ of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], as $
u_X^*\delta_{K_0}$ conjugated by the displayed endpoint isomorphisms. It is invertible and natural in $K$. Changing the witness changes both sides by these natural endpoint isomorphisms; full faithfulness makes the result independent of the witness. Its source is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by Step 1, hence so is its isomorphic target. This uses only the bounded-below etale-origin adjunction, never an adjunction on all pro-etale complexes.

source.place: Proof, actual-adjoint and etale/pro-etale comparison; unit Step 5(c)

proof.text:
Check the orientation normalization. Let $D_0=s(Y)$, viewed also as the zero-section divisor in $P$. Its equations on the standard two affine charts are $t$ and $1$, so the dual ideal generators have transition $t^{-1}$; thus $\mathcal O_P(D_0)=\mathcal O_P(1)$ with the transition convention used in the projective-line class. This follows directly from [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The supported Kummer morphism of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] for this Cartier divisor, after forgetting supports, is therefore $h=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$. On $X$ it is the boundary of the coordinate $t$, and [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies its finite-coefficient realization with the same supported morphism on the pro-etale site. This is the boundary defining $\operatorname{pur}_s$ in [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. The trace of [def-amb-p1-trace] satisfies $t_qh=1$. Hence $\int_p$ sends the image of this supported orientation to $1$. For the proper zero section, the identity-open compactification in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Rs_!=Rs_*$. The canonical composition of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and $ps=\mathrm{id}$ then give $Rp_!Rs_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ on these etale-origin inputs. Composing the two Hom bijections for the zero section and projection, using the composite-counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and $ps=\mathrm{id}$, identifies this evaluation with
$$\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\operatorname{pur}_s}Rs^!\Lambda_X(1)[2]\xrightarrow{Rs^!\gamma_{p,\Lambda}}Rs^!Rp^!\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_Y.$$
It is the identity, which verifies the stated normalization without multiplying the comparison by an unspecified unit.

Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be an arbitrary morphism in the chapter's fixed setting, and write $g_X:X'\to X$, $g_P:P'\to P$, $a',q',p'$ for the pulled-back compactification. No flatness, smoothness, or etaleness is required of $g$. For $L$ bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, all arguments of the following exchange maps are bounded below. On these ordinary etale inputs let $C_p:g^*F_p\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{p'}g_X^*$ be the compact-support exchange and $\tau_L:g_X^*G_pL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{p'}g^*L$ the pullback/twist identification. The isomorphy of $C_p$ on these bounded-below inputs is [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]; the open $a$ is quasi-compact because $P$ is Noetherian. Use the actual compactification formula in [def-cbc-exchange-map]: proper exchange for $q$, followed by open-extension exchange for $a$. The latter is the inverse of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], applied degreewise using [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. The trace and projective-line adjunction normalization commute with base change by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. The root-of-unity twist comparison is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The projection transformations commute with the proper exchange by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]; the open evaluation commutes with pullback because its maps are the identity on the open and zero off it, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Substituting these identities into the explicit counit formula of Step 2 yields the typed equality
$$g^*\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,L}=\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p',g^*L}\circ F_{p'}(\tau_L)\circ C_{p,G_pL}.$$
In particular this checks compatibility of the actual integration counit, not only of the two functors up to isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, arbitrary base change of the defining counit; unit Step 5(c)

proof.text:
Take mates of the equality in Step 7. Use [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to change from the explicit adjunctions to the actual exceptional adjunctions through $\delta,\delta'$. If $\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g}:g_X^*p^\times\to p'^\times g^*$ is the canonical mate of $C_p^{-1}:F_{p'}g_X^*\to g^*F_p$, it is explicitly
$$\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g,L}=p'^\times\!\bigl(g^*\epsilon^{\times}_{p,L}\circ C_{p,p^\times L}^{-1}\bigr)\circ\eta'_{g_X^*p^\times L},$$
where $\eta'$ is the unit of $F_{p'}\dashv p'^\times$ and $\epsilon^{\times}$ is the actual exceptional counit. Its defining counit equation gives
$$\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g,L}\circ g_X^*\delta_L=\delta'_{g^*L}\circ\tau_L.$$
Both sides have the same transpose by Step 7, so equality follows from the adjunction bijection. Now choose the witness $K_0$ of Step 1 and its pullback $g^*K_0$ as witness for $Lg^*K$. The exchange in [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] is explicitly the transport of this ordinary compact-support exchange. The Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and the unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] therefore identify its exceptional mate with the realization of $\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g,K_0}$. Applying $\nu_{X'}^*$ to the preceding equality and using the endpoint identifications of Step 5 gives
$$\beta_{p,g,K}\circ Lg_X^*\gamma_{p,K}=\gamma_{p',Lg^*K}\circ\tau_K.$$
The terms involving $Lg^*K$ are defined in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude]. The two purity comparisons are isomorphisms by Steps 1--5 applied over $Y$ and $Y'$, and $\tau_K$ is an isomorphism, so this equation also proves that the canonical exceptional base-change mate $\beta_{p,g,K}$ is invertible. This is the asserted arbitrary base-change compatibility.

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported paragraph into eight steps. Read the actual normalized projective-line adjunction, composed it with extension by zero, calculated the counit through the finite projection formula, identified its transpose using adjoint uniqueness, realized it through the bounded-below etale-origin comparison, checked the Kummer orientation and wrote the base-change mate equation. Reused existing nodes throughout; no new nodes. The Lean existence declaration contains sorry and does not construct the comparison. Statement unchanged. Second reading restricts the Step 7 input to the bounded constructible finite-Tor scope of the exchange interface.

places: Proof, first four sentences: compose open and projective-line adjunctions and identify the integration counit (Steps 2–4).
Proof, coefficient comparison paragraph: bounded finite etale-origin realization and naturality (Steps 1, 5).
sk-prop-an Step 5(d): zero-section Kummer class and trace normalization (Step 6).
Proof, final base-change sentences: integration counit and exceptional mate (Steps 7–8).

tool_uses.why: Step 1 identifies the prescribed finite pro-etale twist with the ordinary roots-of-unity twist; sk-prop-an uses this coefficient convention but supplies no coefficient-comparison theorem.
Step 1 uses local rank-one freeness for boundedness and Tor amplitude after twisting; the affine-model unit does not construct the coefficient line.
Step 1 chooses a bounded constructible etale witness for the intrinsic pro-etale input; the affine-model unit does not prove site comparison.
Step 1 reflects the finite Tor interval onto the etale witness before applying the etale projection formula; this is a coefficient-comparison tool absent from the affine-model unit.
Steps 1 and 8 preserve bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude under the relevant scheme pullbacks; no exceptional preservation is assumed.
Steps 2 and 7 use the actual normalized projective-line counit and its base-change compatibility, the explicit projective-line input required by unit Step 5(c).
Step 2 uses the whole-derived-category open adjunction to restrict the projective-line adjunction as required by unit Step 5(c).
Step 3 uses the finite-coefficient etale projection isomorphism for p and the open immersion, precisely the projection-formula tool required by unit Step 5(c).
Steps 3 and 7 use the explicit open evaluation to check tensor and base-change compatibility, which the model unit leaves implicit.
Step 3 uses the proper projection isomorphism and its naturality with respect to the open evaluation map; the model unit invokes that projection formula without proving it.
Step 4 compares with the actual ordinary right adjoint; its general existence is a generic framework input, not part of the affine-model calculation.
Step 5 identifies compact supports on bounded-below etale witnesses with their pro-etale realizations; no such comparison is proved by the affine-model unit.
Steps 5 and 8 use the bounded-below comparison unit and full faithfulness, preserving the ordinary/pro-etale distinction required by the model conventions.
Steps 5 and 8 use the actual relative exceptional Hom bijection on etale-origin inputs; the model unit assumes this six-functor interface.
Step 5 realizes the etale isomorphism by exact comparison pullback; the affine-model unit does not establish exactness of that comparison.
Step 5 identifies realization of the derived tensor product using a theorem valid for the comparison ringed topoi, a generic monoidal-pullback tool.
Step 6 forgets supports of the ordinary Cartier Kummer boundary to obtain c1(O(D0)); this is the generic supported-class fact needed by unit Step 5(d).
Step 6 identifies the supported class after finite pro-etale realization with its ordinary-etale witness; the model unit does not prove this coefficient bridge.
Step 6 uses exactly the global coordinate Kummer-boundary orientation required by unit Step 5(d), supplied by the rank-one unit.
Step 7 uses ordinary-etale open-extension base change to compute the specified compact-support exchange; this is the generic compact-support tool of unit Step 5(c).
Step 7 applies the open-extension comparison degreewise to complexes, using this generic exactness theorem.
Step 7 uses the canonical roots-of-unity/twist pullback isomorphism for arbitrary g, a generic coefficient tool not an affine-purity conclusion.
Step 7 uses the exact projection/exchange commutative square to check the counit equation, rather than asserting an unspecified compatibility.
Step 8 uses that the specific pro-etale compact-support exchange on witnessed objects is the transported ordinary exchange, as required by the model base-change clause.

Step 1 bounds the absolute dimension of P by applying the finite-type fibre bound over Spec k; this checks the dimension hypothesis of the generic actual-adjoint comparison without assuming Y is regular.
Step 6 needs the canonical compact-support composition for p followed by its proper zero section in order to type the normalization transpose.
